memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'This is what it means,' Joseph said. 'The three baskets are three days. Within three days Pharaoh will lift off your head and impale your body on a pole. And the birds will eat away your flesh.'" - Gen 40:18-19 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Joseph now has to deliver a terrible message. The baker's dream did not mean restoration; it meant death within three days. And Joseph tells him the truth — plainly, without softening it, even though it must have been agonizing to say. He does not flatter the man or bend the message to spare his feelings. He speaks what God had revealed, hard as it was.

This took a different kind of courage than resisting temptation. It is one thing to give someone good news; it is another to look a man in the eye and tell him what he does not want to hear. Joseph could have hedged, or made the interpretation vague, or offered false comfort. Instead, he was faithful to the truth.

There is an important lesson here about integrity. A faithful messenger of God tells the whole truth, not just the pleasant parts. Whether the news is welcome or unwelcome, we are called to be honest. Sometimes love itself requires telling a hard truth rather than a comfortable lie. "Faithful are the wounds of a friend" (Prov 27:6).

Of course, hard truths must always be spoken with compassion, not cruelty. Joseph did not gloat; he simply told the man what was coming. May God give us both the courage to speak truth when it is difficult and the tenderness to speak it with love. Truth and kindness are meant to walk together.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I willing to tell a hard truth when it is needed?
2. Do I speak truth with compassion, not cruelty?
3. Where might love require me to be honest rather than comfortable?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, give me courage to speak the truth even when it is hard, and tenderness to speak it with love. Keep me from both flattering lies and cruel words. Help me to be faithful and kind. Amen.
